name: Brody Myopathy

criteria.description: Impaired muscle relaxation during or immediately after exercise
Electromyography showing silent contractures without myotonic discharges
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the ATP2A1 gene
Absence of clinical or electrical myotonia
Muscle biopsy showing selective type II fiber atrophy and reduced SERCA1 expression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of impaired muscle relaxation during exercise, characteristic electromyography findings, and identification of ATP2A1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by clinical presentation and exclusion of other myopathies with myotonia.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of myotonia despite delayed relaxation

common.symptomName: Muscle stiffness during or after exercise
Difficulty releasing grip after sustained contraction

laboratory: Normal serum creatine kinase levels or mildly elevated
Absence of myotonic discharges on electromyography
imaging: Muscle MRI may show selective involvement of type II fibers
Muscle biopsy demonstrating type II fiber atrophy and reduced SERCA1 expression
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in ATP2A1 gene encoding SERCA1
other: Electromyography showing silent contractures without myotonia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of clinical and electrical myotonia
Multisystem involvement including cataracts and cardiac conduction defects
CTG repeat expansion in DMPK gene
Paradoxical myotonia worsened by repeated activity and cold exposure
Congenital myopathy with muscle weakness and hypotonia
Characteristic central cores on muscle biopsy

redFlags: Progressive muscle weakness beyond typical Brody myopathy course
Presence of myotonia on clinical or EMG examination
Cardiac symptoms such as arrhythmias or conduction defects
references: Brody, E. N. (1969). A familial myopathy with impairment of muscle relaxation. Neurology, 19(7), 633-640.
Krause, T., et al. (2004). Brody myopathy is caused by mutations in ATP2A1, encoding the fast-twitch skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase SERCA1. Nature Genetics, 36(2), 144-149.
